title: Governor-Generals & Viceroys
subject: History (CDS/NDA)

blocks.heading: 🎩 Governor-Generals & Viceroys
blocks.intro: The administrative heads of British rule in India who designed expansionist and reformist policies.

blocks.heading: 1. Governor-Generals of Bengal (1773 - 1833)
bullets: Warren Hastings (1773-1785): First GG of Bengal. Ended Dual Government. Established civil/criminal courts. Impeached in London (later acquitted).
Lord Cornwallis (1786-1793): Father of Civil Services in India. Introduced **Permanent Settlement (Zamindari)** in Bengal (1793). Created Cornwallis Code (separating judiciary and executive).
Lord Wellesley (1798-1805): Introduced **Subsidiary Alliance System** (Hyderabad first to sign in 1798). Called himself "Bengal Tiger".

blocks.heading: 2. Governor-Generals of India (1833 - 1858)
bullets: Lord William Bentinck (1828-1835): First GG of India. Social Reforms: **Abolished Sati (1829, Regulation XVII)** with help of Raja Ram Mohan Roy. Suppressed Thuggee cult. Introduced English as medium of higher education (Macaulay's Minute 1835).

blocks.heading: 3. Viceroys of India (1858 - 1947)
bullets: Lord Canning (1856-1862): First Viceroy. Suppressed 1857 Revolt. Ended East India Company rule (GoI Act 1858). Abolished Doctrine of Lapse. Introduced portfolio system.
Lord Lytton (1876-1880): Vernacular Press Act (1878 - censored local papers), Arms Act (1878). Grand Delhi Durbar (1877) amid famine.

Lord Ripon (1880-1884): Liberal Viceroy. Repealed Vernacular Press Act. Father of **Local Self-Government** in India. Passed first Factory Act (1881). Ilbert Bill Controversy (proposed allowing Indian judges to try Europeans). First synchronous census (1881).
Lord Curzon (1899-1905): Partitioned Bengal (1905) on communal lines, sparking Swadeshi movement. Established Archaeological Survey of India.
Lord Mountbatten (1947-1948): Last Viceroy. Planned partition (3rd June Plan). First GG of independent India.

formulas: Sati Abolished: 1829 (Bentinck) | Railways: 1853 (Dalhousie) | Local Self-Gov: Ripon | Bengal Partition: 1905 (Curzon)
